trials.notes: Correctly used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), next_tag('H1'), a depth-bounded next_token() subtree walk, get_token_type() === '#text', and get_modifiable_text(). All called APIs are documented; no _doing_it_wrong records. Handles nested text, decoded entities, image-only H1, no H1, multiple H1s, and unclosed H1.

Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor and used only documented APIs: create_fragment(), next_token(), get_token_type(), is_tag_closer(), get_tag(), get_current_depth(), and get_modifiable_text(). The outer next_token() scan plus inner subtree walk is acceptable here because it returns after the first H1; the documented nested-loop caution does not create a defect for a single region.

Same strong pattern as the reference: HTML Processor fragment parsing, next_tag('h1'), recorded depth, next_token() walk, #text guard, decoded get_modifiable_text(). Lowercase tag query is consistent with documented examples and behavior. No undocumented calls or misuse.

failure_analysis: All trials passed all 8 hidden cases, so there are no per-case failures to attribute. The docs did especially well in three places: the processor-selection guidance says to use WP_HTML_Processor when structure matters, including collecting element text and handling missing closing tags; the “Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree” gives the exact create_fragment + next_tag + depth-bounded next_token + #text + get_modifiable_text pattern; and the get_current_depth()/next_token() docs explicitly explain virtual closers, malformed input, and why the subtree guard must use >= rather than >. The get_modifiable_text() docs also clearly state that #text values are already decoded, which prevented double-decoding or raw entity output. Near-misses: trial-2 used nested next_token() loops, which the docs warn against for repeated regions, but the function returns after the first region so no sibling is skipped. Trial-3 relied on lowercase next_tag('h1'); examples imply this is fine, but the next_tag contract could state case-insensitive tag-name matching more directly.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs show lowercase examples but do not explicitly state that tag-name queries are case-insensitive while get_tag() returns uppercase names.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a sentence to the tag_name query description: tag-name matching is ASCII case-insensitive; callers comparing get_tag() results should compare against uppercase normalized names.

doc_gaps.location: html-processor.md / Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree
doc_gaps.problem: The recipe says to append #text tokens, but it does not explicitly spell out the result for a matched element with no text descendants.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general note that a successfully matched container with no ordinary #text descendants accumulates an empty string, while absence of the container is a separate caller policy.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs distinguish #text tokens from special-element opener text, but they do not directly state that attribute values such as img alt/title are not DOM text descendants.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short note that attributes are not included in ordinary subtree text; read attributes explicitly only when the caller asks for attribute-derived text.

doc_gaps.problem: The completion-policy language is accurate but spread across the overview, next_token(), and get_current_depth() sections.
doc_gaps.suggestion: In the subtree text recipe, add one compact example note showing that unclosed ordinary elements still produce virtual closers and can yield best-effort text, while paused_at_incomplete_token() and get_last_error() remain separate policy checks.
